title: YouTube Comments
summary: Gets every comment and reply on a YouTube video with yt-dlp, then turns them into threads for analysis or a vibe-dashboard.
what_it_is: A Claude skill for pulling the **complete** comment tree of a YouTube video, every top-level comment and every reply, with the thread structure intact.

The download runs on Swami's Mac with the free yt-dlp tool, either directly or through Swami's ytx shortcut, or on a Windows PC with yt-dlp in PowerShell (no API key, no video download). The resulting `.info.json` file is uploaded, and Claude does all of the processing: counts, a threaded text file, and the hand-off to a dashboard, table, or export.
why: YouTube lazy-loads comments and hides replies behind "show more replies". Copying by hand on the FORTH video captured 75 of 474 comments (about 16%), with whole reply chains missing and no way to tell. yt-dlp gets everything in one pass.

what_it_does.text: Gives Swami the ytx one-liner, or the yt-dlp commands with the real video URL and a short folder name already filled in, ready to paste.
Pulls every comment and reply, sorted the way the YouTube page shows them (`comment_sort=top`), with no reply-depth limit.
Reports title, channel, views, upload date, the page's comment count versus the number extracted, top-level comments, replies, unique authors, and uploader replies.

Writes `comments-threaded.txt`: threads ranked by total likes, replies in time order, uploader replies marked. A reply to a reply stays in its thread and is marked "(reply to @handle)", so no reply is dropped.

Hands off to the vibe-dashboard skill's comment-dashboard layout: Claude writes the standard comment JSON (6 to 9 topics, always with Chatter, plus themes credited to specific @handles), and vibe-dashboard's `comments_sections.py` builds The Video, Comments at a Glance, Themes & Takeaways, and one Comment Threads table of every comment and reply, opening sorted by Topic. A Method section adds the command, counts, and date pulled.
One row per comment with the @handle linked to the comment's permalink, text, likes, and a sentiment tag.
Sends the threaded text file, or a CSV or Excel file built with the xlsx skill.
Only with Swami's OK, and only when yt-dlp and ytx can't run: a browser-console script loads and expands the comments for copying (partial: reply nesting is flattened).

triggers: "Get the comments from this video: <YouTube URL>"
"Make a dashboard of the comments on <YouTube URL>"

how_to_use.step: Give Claude the YouTube link and say what you want: a dashboard, a table, or the raw comments.

If yt-dlp is not on the Mac yet, install the standalone `yt-dlp_macos` binary to `/usr/local/bin/yt-dlp` (Claude gives the four commands), then ytx (see the youtube-transcript skill). Check with `yt-dlp --version` and `ytx -v`.

Quickest: `ytx -c "VIDEO_URL"`, or copy the link, double-click **YouTube Transcript** on the Desktop, and answer y for comments. Or paste Claude's yt-dlp commands (folder `~/yt/SHORTNAME`, `--skip-download --write-comments --write-info-json`). It may sit quiet for a minute or more. Claude never runs the extraction itself, even in a linked chat.

Upload the `TITLE [VIDEOID].info.json` file from that folder to the chat (it is often over 1 MB). In a chat linked to your computer, Claude can read it from your `~/yt` folder instead, once you grant access.
Claude loads the file, prints the stats, and writes `comments-threaded.txt`.
Claude builds the dashboard (vibe-dashboard skill), the table, or the export.

skills.name: vibe-dashboard
skills.why: Builds the comments dashboard, the usual goal, with its comment-dashboard layout and `comments_sections.py`. Needed only for dashboards.

skills.name: xlsx
skills.why: Builds a CSV or Excel export when asked. Anthropic's built-in skill.

skills.name: youtube-transcript
skills.why: A sibling skill for a video's transcript and chapters; it documents installing ytx, which this skill uses as its shortcut. Not called by this skill.

programs.name: yt-dlp
programs.why: Downloads the comments and video metadata into the `.info.json` file.
programs.install: Use the standalone `yt-dlp_macos` binary (bundles its own Python). Needs macOS 10.15 or newer. Update with `sudo yt-dlp -U` when extraction breaks.
programs.install_windows: `winget install yt-dlp.yt-dlp` (also installs Deno and FFmpeg), or `yt-dlp.exe` from the releases page on the PATH. Update with `winget upgrade yt-dlp.yt-dlp` or `yt-dlp -U`.

programs.name: ytx
programs.why: Swami's one-step wrapper around yt-dlp: `ytx -c URL` (or the Desktop **YouTube Transcript** icon) pulls the comments and writes `comments-threaded.txt`.
programs.install: A custom Bash script installed to `/usr/local/bin/ytx`; setup steps are in the youtube-transcript skill. Needs yt-dlp and `python3`.
programs.install_windows: `ytx.ps1`, the PowerShell port (same commands and output, no Python). Save it to Downloads, then run `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$HOME\Downloads\ytx.ps1" -Install`, reopen PowerShell, and run `ytx -SelfTest`.

programs.name: Deno
programs.why: The JavaScript runtime yt-dlp uses to solve YouTube's challenges. Comments-only pulls have worked without it on the Mac (the warning is safe to ignore); install it if extraction fails.
programs.install: Not installed on the Mac today. If needed, install from docs.deno.com (version 2.3 or newer).
programs.install_windows: Comes with `winget install yt-dlp.yt-dlp`. With a manual `yt-dlp.exe`, put `deno.exe` (2.3 or newer) on the PATH or next to `yt-dlp.exe`.

programs.name: Terminal / PowerShell
programs.why: Runs the install and extraction commands.
programs.install: Built into macOS. Installing uses `sudo`, so an admin password is needed once.
programs.install_windows: Use PowerShell, built into Windows 10 and 11. Commands go one per line, with no `sudo`.

programs.name: Python 3
programs.why: Processes the uploaded JSON into stats and threads.
programs.install: Already there when Claude's code execution is on.

programs.name: Web browser
programs.why: Only for the fallback console script.
programs.install: Any desktop browser with developer tools (F12).
programs.install_windows: Same: any desktop browser with developer tools (F12).

capabilities.text: Every top-level comment and every reply, with parent links, in one pass. Replies to replies are walked up to their top-level comment, so they land in the right thread.
No YouTube API key, no Google account, and no video download.
Each comment carries author, text, likes, timestamp, uploader flag, and pinned flag.
Any comment can be linked directly: `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEOID&lc=COMMENTID`.
On a dashboard, every comment and reply sits in one Comment Threads table (Topic / From / QTY / QTY-TOT / Likes / Comment / Link) with a ↗ link to the exact comment on YouTube.

limitations.text: Claude's cloud workspace usually cannot reach youtube.com, and neither can a linked computer's sandboxed shell, so the download always runs on your Mac or PC, by you.
The comment count YouTube shows rarely matches the number extracted, because its counter drifts as comments are held or removed. Both numbers are reported.
YouTube changes often break older yt-dlp versions; updating usually fixes it.
The browser-console fallback flattens reply nesting and may miss comments, so Claude offers it only with your OK, when yt-dlp and ytx can't run.
ytx.ps1 1.2.0 was rebuilt from the Mac script and has never been run on a real Windows PC. Its built-in `ytx -SelfTest` checks its results against the Mac ytx.

The `comments-threaded.txt` that ytx 1.2.0 writes still groups replies by parent only, so it can miss replies to replies. Claude re-threads from the `.info.json`, which is complete, so dashboards are not affected. A ytx fix is pending.

scheduled_tasks.summary: None. The skill runs on request and does not need or create any scheduled tasks.

runs_in.where: Claude app, cloud session (web, desktop, mobile)
runs_in.notes: Swami runs yt-dlp on the Mac and uploads the `.info.json`; Claude does the rest. Needs code execution on.

runs_in.where: Claude desktop app linked to the Mac
runs_in.notes: Claude can read the files from your `~/yt` folder once you grant it access, so there's no upload step. It can't run ytx or yt-dlp there: the linked computer's shell is a sandboxed workspace that sees only connected folders, not your Mac's Terminal. You still run the extraction.

runs_in.where: Claude desktop app linked to a Windows PC
runs_in.notes: Claude could read the `.info.json` from your connected `yt` folder, but can't run the PowerShell commands through the linked PC's sandboxed shell; you run them. Not tried yet.
Processing works if the `.info.json` is already on the phone; the extraction itself needs a computer.
Should run yt-dlp directly in the terminal, since Claude Code runs on the Mac itself.

other_ais.notes: Skills need a Business, Enterprise, Edu, or Healthcare plan. Extraction still runs on the Mac; processing needs ChatGPT's code tool. Swami tests in Claude only.
Upload the unzipped skill folder. Processing needs code execution; the dashboard hand-off also needs the vibe-dashboard skill installed there. Swami tests in Claude only.
Import the .zip (or the SKILL.md if refused). Installing by chat tends to drift from the original; add the skill directly. Swami tests in Claude only.

gotchas.text: `max_comments` takes five values: total, parents, replies, replies per thread, and depth. A depth of 1 silently discards every reply, so always pass `all,all,all,all,all`.

A reply to a reply names the earlier reply as its parent, not the thread. Grouping by parent alone drops it silently (ytx 1.2.0 did this on a real video in Nov 2026). The skill's own processing code walks each reply up to its thread; check that the replies printed equal the replies counted.
The plain `yt-dlp` download needs Python 3.10 or newer, and the Mac has 3.9. Use the standalone `yt-dlp_macos` binary.
If macOS blocks it as from an unidentified developer, run `sudo xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /usr/local/bin/yt-dlp`.
yt-dlp's default sort is newest first; the skill sets `comment_sort=top` to match the YouTube page.
The extraction can print nothing for a minute or more while it pages through comments. That is normal.
A warning about a missing JavaScript runtime is safe to ignore for a comments-only pull.
Don't retry the download from Claude's workspace with curl or another route; the network allowlist blocks it.
A chat linked to your computer gets a sandboxed workspace there, not your Mac's Terminal. It has no ytx and usually can't reach YouTube, so you run the extraction yourself.
A `~/yt/<video-id>/` folder left by a transcript run without `-c` has no comments in its `.info.json`. Run `ytx -c "VIDEO_URL"` to download it again with comments.
In Nov 2026 a chat switched to the app's browser on its own when it found no comments. The skill now forbids that: Claude must ask first, since the browser route is partial.
Uploads may have spaces and brackets replaced with underscores; the processing script's file match handles that.
YouTube changed again: run `sudo yt-dlp -U`, then retry the `ytx -c` command.
Windows SmartScreen may block a downloaded `yt-dlp.exe` with "Windows protected your PC". Choose **More info › Run anyway**.
The Mac commands use a backslash to continue a line; PowerShell doesn't. On Windows, paste each command as one line.
After `winget install`, close and reopen PowerShell before `yt-dlp` is found.
If extraction starts failing with a JavaScript-runtime error, install Deno (winget installs already include it).

On Windows the `ytx` command runs through a `.cmd` file, which may cut a link at `&` (for example `watch?v=…&t=30s`). ytx still gets the video, but a stray error line may follow; use the Desktop icon, `ytx -p`, or the youtu.be share link.

requirements.text: macOS 10.15 or newer with an admin password for the one-time install, or Windows 10 or 11 with PowerShell.
Claude's code execution ("Create and edit files") must be on to process the JSON.
Upload the `.info.json` file to the chat, unless the chat is linked and Claude reads it from your `~/yt` folder.
The Mac or PC needs to reach YouTube, and GitHub for the first download of yt-dlp.
The vibe-dashboard skill must be installed to build a comments dashboard.

glossary.def: A free command-line tool that downloads videos and their metadata, including comments, from YouTube and many other sites.
The macOS app for typing commands; used for the install and extraction on a Mac (PowerShell on Windows).
Swami's command-line tool that wraps yt-dlp: a Bash script on the Mac and ytx.ps1, a PowerShell port, on Windows. `ytx -c` pulls a video's comments into a yt folder along with a threaded text file.
The macOS security check that blocks downloaded apps from unidentified developers until approved.
A file attribute macOS adds to downloads; removing it lets Gatekeeper run the file.
Runs a Terminal command with administrator rights; it asks for the Mac's admin password.
The JSON file yt-dlp writes with the video's metadata and, with --write-comments, its full comments array.
A top-level comment together with all of its replies.
A direct link to one comment, built from the video ID and the comment ID.
A reply written by the video's own channel, flagged author_is_uploader in the data.
yt-dlp's five-part limit on comments: total, parents, replies, replies per thread, and depth.
yt-dlp's comment order setting; top matches what the YouTube page shows, new is yt-dlp's default.
Claude's ability to run code and create files, which this skill needs for processing.

The shell Claude gets when a chat is linked to Swami's Mac through the desktop app. It is a sandboxed workspace that sees only connected folders, not the Mac's Terminal, so it can read the files but can't run ytx or yt-dlp.
The private Linux machine Claude works in; its network is allowlisted, so it usually cannot reach youtube.com.
Swami's skill that builds dark-theme, single-file HTML dashboards; this skill hands its data to it.
A short code computed from the skill's files; it changes whenever the skill changes, flagging this page as out of date.
The command-line shell built into Windows 10 and 11; it runs the Windows install and extraction commands.
Windows' built-in package manager; installs and updates yt-dlp with one command.
The Windows security check that warns before running downloaded programs from unrecognized publishers.
A JavaScript runtime that yt-dlp uses to solve YouTube's JavaScript challenges.
vibe-dashboard's shared format for comment and review data: source, labels, topics, themes, and one item per comment or reply.
vibe-dashboard's script that turns the standard comment JSON into The Video, Comments at a Glance, Themes & Takeaways, and Comment Threads sections.
In the Comment Threads table, the number of messages in the whole thread; QTY counts only those in the thread with the same topic.

spoken._intro: This page is the skill sheet for the YouTube comments skill. It gets every comment and reply on a YouTube video with the free tool why-tee-dee-ell-pee, or Swami's YTX shortcut on a Mac or Windows PC, then turns them into threads for analysis or a vibe dashboard.
spoken.What It Is: What the skill is, and why it exists: copying comments by hand once caught only seventy five of four hundred and seventy four
spoken.What It Does: Eight things it handles, from ready to paste commands and full extraction, to stats, a threaded text file that keeps replies to replies in their thread, a dashboard with one table of every comment sorted by topic, a table, an export, and a browser fallback
spoken.How to Use It: What to ask for, then six steps on the Mac: ask, install once, [extract](/ɪkstɹˈækt/) with YTX or why-tee-dee-ell-pee yourself, [upload](/ʌplˈoʊd/) the file or let Claude read it from a linked Mac, let Claude process it, and choose the hand off. A second table gives the same steps on Windows, with the PowerShell version of YTX
spoken.Skills It Depends On: None are required. The vibe dashboard skill is used for dashboards, the XLSX skill for spreadsheet exports, and the YouTube transcript skill is a related sibling that explains how to install YTX
spoken.Programs It Depends On: Why-tee-dee-ell-pee and Swami's YTX shortcut, which now has a PowerShell version for Windows, plus Terminal or PowerShell, Python in Claude's workspace, and optionally [Deno](/dˈiːnoʊ/) and a web browser. Each program has macOS and Windows install notes
spoken.Capabilities and Limitations: It gets the complete comment tree with no API key, keeps replies to replies in their threads, and on a dashboard puts every comment in one table. But neither Claude's cloud workspace nor a linked computer's shell can reach YouTube, comment counts drift, YouTube changes can break older versions, the browser fallback is partial and needs Swami's OK, and the Windows YTX has never been run
spoken.Scheduled Tasks: None. The skill runs only when asked
spoken.Where It Runs: It works in any Claude app session with code execution on. In a chat linked to the Mac, Claude can read the file but can't run the extraction, so that's partial. A linked Windows PC, Claude Code, and other AI assistants are not tested; Swami tests in Claude only
spoken.Gotchas: Eighteen traps, the biggest being that a reply depth of one silently drops every reply, and that grouping replies by parent alone drops replies to replies. Three cover linked computers, folders without comments, and never switching to the browser on its own; four are for Windows, and one covers a missing [Deno](/dˈiːnoʊ/)
spoken.Other Requirements: A Mac running macOS ten fifteen or newer, or a Windows ten or eleven PC, plus code execution, a way to [upload](/ʌplˈoʊd/) the file, and internet on the computer
spoken.Card and Freshness: Which version of the skill this page describes and its fingerprint

how_to_use_windows.step: Give Claude the YouTube link, say you're on Windows, and say what you want.

In PowerShell: `winget install yt-dlp.yt-dlp` (also installs Deno and FFmpeg). Then install ytx: save `ytx.ps1` to Downloads and run `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$HOME\Downloads\ytx.ps1" -Install`. Reopen PowerShell and check `ytx -v` and `ytx -SelfTest`.

Quickest: `ytx -c "VIDEO_URL"`, or copy the link, double-click **YouTube Transcript** on the Desktop, and answer y for comments. Without ytx, paste Claude's two PowerShell yt-dlp lines (folder `$HOME\yt\SHORTNAME`).
Claude loads the file, prints the stats, and writes `comments-threaded.txt`, the same as on the Mac.
Dashboard, table, or export, the same as on the Mac.
